title: Data Center Power and Cooling System Support
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) Procurement Office: The Mission and Installation Contracting Command (MICC), Yuma Proving Ground (MICC-YPG), is currently conducting market research to bolster Government and industry coordination and partnership in support of the Department of Information Management (DoIM) at the United States Army Yuma Proving Ground (USAYPG), Arizona. Respondents are strongly encouraged to provide thorough answers to all questions outlined in this RFI and to explicitly address the relevant sections of the PWS within their submissions. If applicable, please provide: Contract number or customer name Total contract value Period of performance Brief synopsis of the scope of the work performed (2) Is your company capable of providing the services described in the attached draft PWS? (5) Does industry agree that the use of NAICS code 541513, Computer Facilities Management Services, is the best fit for this requirement? If not, please suggest an alternative and explain why. (6) What is your firm�s size and status under NAICS 541513? Please identify whether your firm is a small business and any applicable socioeconomic category or contract vehicle. (7) If your company cannot perform this requirement, please identify the primary reasons why. THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) is issued solely for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. This is not a Request for Quote (RFQ), and the Government is not seeking quotes at this time. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI; all costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party�s expense. Responses to this notice will be used for market research purposes only. The Government is interested in input from the small business community, as well as other interested sources, regarding their capability to meet the requirement. Small businesses in all socioeconomic categories are encouraged to identify their capabilities in meeting the requirement. INFORMATION: The proposed requirement is anticipated to be classified under NAICS 541513, Computer Facilities Management Services. title: V--International Expedited Freight Forwarding Service
description: Posted Date: September 8, 2026 Procurement Office: The Department of the Interior (DOI) � Interior Business Center (IBC), Acquisition Services Directorate (AQD) Response Due Date: September 23, 2026, at 1000 AM EST NOTICE OF INTENT SYNOPSIS: The DOI, IBC, AQD on behalf of Peace Corps� Office of Operations & Security intends to award three Contracts to Cavalier, EWC, and DBA, on a sole source basis for International Expedited Freight Forwarding Services. These Contracts are anticipated to include a 12-month base period and four 12-month Option Periods. The intended procurement is classified under North American Industry Classification System code (NAICS) Code 488510 � Freight Transportation Arrangement. This is a Sole Source procurement under the authority of Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 12 � Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. There are only three responsible sources, and no other services will satisfy agency requirements. Description of Requirement: The Peace Corps Office of Operations & Security (Facilities Management Division) requires specialized international 4PL freight-forwarding, logistics, and customs-brokerage services for shipments originating from Peace Corps Headquarters to overseas Peace Corps posts in more than 60 countries. This requirement directly supports Volunteer health, safety, and operational infrastructure. Primary shipment categories include: � Temperature-Sensitive Medical Logistics: Pharmaceuticals, vaccines, biological materials, and prescription medications requiring continuous temperature maintenance (+2�C to +8�C, -20�C, and -80�C). � Dangerous Goods: IATA Class 9 hazardous materials, including non-removable lithium-ion batteries installed in IT and medical diagnostic units. � Diplomatic Cargo: Cargo requiring U.S. Department of State (DoS) Government Bills of Lading (GBL) and handoff into diplomatic pouch/cargo chains of custody. Peace Corps operating experience, shipping procedures, and market research to date � including review of vendor corporate history, public regulatory filings, and documented service capabilities � demonstrate that standard commercial parcel services do not provide the combined capability required for this requirement, particularly active cold-chain recovery during transit disruptions, specialized pharmaceutical customs support, and integration with Department of State diplomatic freight processes. Market research and Peace Corps operating experience identify three proposed sources as providing distinct capabilities relevant to the Government's minimum need: Cavalier Logistics, Expedited World Cargo (EWC), and Distribution by Air (DBA)/Radiant Logistics. Therefore, this requirement will be established as three BPAs, one each set up as a sole source to each of these vendors, based on the following rationale: � Common couriers do not offer end-to-end active cold-chain custody, in-transit dry-ice replenishment, or re-icing during flight interruptions or customs holds. In addition, standard commercial couriers generally leave destination customs clearance to the receiving Post. At many Posts, staff do not have the specialized brokerage relationships, pharmaceutical import expertise, or regulatory infrastructure necessary to resolve complex Ministry of Health and customs requirements within the validated cold-chain hold period. Failure to maintain temperature control during transit disruptions results in irreversible product excursion, complete inventory loss, and mission failure through delayed medical treatment for Volunteers. � Cavalier is the only source presently documented as providing this complete logistics model. Under Peace Corps' established cold-chain procedure, the Government maintains the required temperature only through the domestic transfer to Cavalier's Sterling, Virginia operation, after which Cavalier assumes responsibility for maintaining the temperature-controlled environment throughout the international movement, including access to temperature-controlled holding and the ability to restore the shipment's validated temperature-control configuration when necessary. Peace Corps' shipping decision matrix places Cavalier as the primary option for seasonal and short-expiry cold-chain shipments, with EWC identified only as a conditional alternative when the receiving Post is reachable and the applicable service guarantee is adequate, and the matrix specifically notes Cavalier's replacement guarantee. � EWC's primary differentiating value is customs, regulatory compliance, and difficult-destination logistics. Its in-house customs brokerage, government and Embassy experience, dangerous-goods capability, and international agent network provide an independent solution for shipments in which destination clearance, import regulations, or local logistics conditions present the principal operational risk. EWC's government/embassy role is distinct from DBA's: EWC's specialization addresses destination-side customs and regulatory clearance � navigating host-nation import requirements and difficult or post-conflict markets � rather than DBA's defense-credentialed secure packaging and transport function. � DBA's specialized value to Peace Corps is hazardous-material transportation and secure Government freight rather than active pharmaceutical cold-chain logistics. DBA's extensive dangerous-goods experience, federal transportation credentials, military/government freight expertise, and access to the broader Radiant carrier network provide an independent capability for Class 9 and other regulated shipments where airline acceptance, routing restrictions, carrier capacity, or destination conditions constrain ordinary transportation options. DBA holds a documented federal credential portfolio � including ITAR registration, DoD-approved carrier status, Civil Reserve Air Fleet carrier designation, AECA compliance, C-TPAT certification, and GSA-approved Transportation Service Provider status � supporting military-spec cargo packaging and secure transport of State Department-regulated cargo (e.g., gas detectors, lithium-battery equipment, and other non-cold-chain HAZMAT). In summation, Cavalier provides the Agency's sole documented full active cold-chain and diplomatic-integration capability for the most technically demanding shipments. DBA and EWC each provide independent, non-overlapping specialized networks � secure defense-credentialed transport and destination-side customs/compliance clearance, respectively � reducing the operational risk associated with dependence on a single international logistics network in a volatile global transit environment. Period of Performance: One 12-month Base Period and four 12-month Option Periods. Response Information: This action is being processed in accordance with 41U.S.C 1901 as implemented by RFO 12.102(b). This notice of intent to award a sole source contracts is NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. A SOLICITATION WILL NOT BE ISSUED. However, all responsible sources that feel they can meet the Government's requirements detailed above may submit a capability statement which shall be considered by the agency. title: Ultra Highspeed Megapixel CMOS Imaging Camera
description: This acquisition is to purchase of a ultra high speed megapixel CMOS imaging camera (PHANTOM VEO 1310L, MONO 72GB MEMORY) from Vision Research Inc. The ultra high speed imaging camera from Vision Research will be used in experiments that will be performed by the Cellular Neurophysiology Section at the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (CNS/NINDS). The experiments being performed will directly test the effects of alterations in neural circuitry in various animal models of Parkinson�s Disease. Specifically, we are interested in understanding how synaptic and intrinsic conductances expressed on these neurons differ among subpopulations dopamine neurons. We are also interested in understanding how the synaptic and circuit connections onto these cells control their activity and ultimately how they contribute to dopamine dependent behaviors and dysfunction. The hope that this information may provide insight to why SNc dopamine neurons are particularly vulnerable in Parkinson�s disease. Our goal is to identify novel physiological and genetic markers in single SNc dopamine neurons which may be useful in defining subpopulations of these neurons. To study the circuits that control midbrain dopaminergic neurons, experimenters in the Cellular Neurophysiology Section prepare tissue slices that will be mounted on an electrophysiology setup. Although electrophysiological recordings provide high temporal resolution and require highly specialized knowledge in order to have consistent success. To increase the successful acquisition of this information, we will use an imaging system that will allow us to perform imaging using fluorescent voltage indicators in which the fluorescence intensity correlate to the neuronal membrane voltage. The major component of this system is a high speed camera that is highly sensitive to moderately low light levels and can also image at frame rates that reach at 10 kilohertz or above. This requirement is necessary because action potentials occur at 1 ms. Using the voltage imaging approach, we will be able to image large populations of neurons, tens to hundreds, simultaneously which is not possible using standard electrophysiology approaches such as patch clamp. Lastly, the camera should have the lowest pixel noise possible so that signal to noise ratio can be maximized for use voltage-indicators that have only small changes fluorescence changes in their signal.

title: Auto Droplet Generator
description: The Diabetes Molecular Genetics Section of the Phoenix Epidemiology and Clinical Research Branch at the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK) studies pancreatic islet organoids derived from induced pluripotent stem cells to investigate molecular pathways associated with type 2 diabetes. The laboratory recently acquired a QX600 Droplet Digital Polymerase Chain Reaction system to generate cell type-specific gene expression data, perform methylation analysis for epigenomic studies, and estimate pancreatic islet composition using cell type-specific marker genes. Currently, the laboratory uses a Manual Droplet Generator to prepare samples for droplet digital polymerase chain reaction analysis. Although the system can process up to eight samples at a time, preparation of a full 96-well plate is time-consuming and relies heavily on manual pipetting. The Auto Droplet Generator shall automate droplet generation for droplet digital polymerase chain reaction workflows, reduce hands-on processing time, and improve throughput and consistency across experiments involving pancreatic islets and islet organoids.

title: Ireland – Laboratory services – Sampling and Analysis of Private Water Supplies in County Wexford
description: As the Supervisory authority for small private regulated water supplies in Wexford, Wexford County Council is required to monitor certain group water schemes and private premises which have their own wells, including caravan parks, schools, estates etc. The drinking water is sampled and analysed in accordance with S.l. No. 99/2023 - European Union (Drinking Water) Regulations 2023. Results are reported to Wexford County Council each month. The current compliance sampling contract ends on December 31st, 2026, and Wexford County Council is requesting tenders from interested parties for provision of these services. The service provider will be required to provide the following services: a) Compliance (and occasional investigative) sampling and analysis of drinking water for both 'check' and 'audit' parameters as set down by S.I. No. 99/2023 - European Union (Drinking Water) Regulations 2023 and listed in Appendix 1 Requirements and specifications. b) Occasional investigative sampling. These are normally duplicate samples i.e coliforms, e.coli free and total chlorine. Other parameters may also be asked for. c) In accordance with EPA requirements, all analysis of parameters in compliance samples (except for free and total chlorine, odour and taste and Dalapon) shall be accredited. Investigative samples do not have to be accredited. d) Reporting of results to Wexford County Council as detailed in Appendix 1 Requirements and specifications. There are currently about 170 private and group water supplies (Entities). This number is variable. It is expected that up to 15 additional schemes will be added during 2026 and these additional entities shall be sampled and analysed at tender rates. Each scheme shall have two check samples carried out annually. A small number of schemes will have more than two check samples and/or will require an audit sample. The level of analysis, including Limits of Detections must meet the requirements cited in S.I. No. 99/2023 - European Union (Drinking Water) Regulations 2023. The laboratory appointed (and/or sub contracted laboratory) must be accredited to !NAB (or equivalent) for all relevant parameters.

title: 6350--VA Police Security System Upgrade (VA-26-00085372)
description: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Technology Acquisition Center (TAC), intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price contract on a sole-source basis to Homefront Security, LLC, an SBA-certified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), under the Veterans First Contracting Program. This requirement is for a Brand Name Pelco Police Enterprise Security System Upgrade supporting the VA New York Harbor Healthcare System (NYHHS) at three facilities: the Margaret Cochran Corbin Campus, Brooklyn VA Medical Center (VAMC), and St. Albans VAMC Community Living Center. The requirement includes the acquisition, installation, configuration, integration, testing, commissioning, documentation, and warranty support necessary to upgrade the existing enterprise physical security system. The effort includes replacement and expansion of Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) infrastructure, enterprise video analytics, network connectivity between campuses, replacement of cellular alarm communicators, and integration with the Medical Center s existing Pelco Video Management System (VMS). Delivery of the Brand Name Pelco Security System Upgrade shall be completed within 60 days of award. Installation, configuration, integration, programming, commissioning, testing, and documentation shall be completed within 120 days of award. This acquisition is being conducted under the Veterans First Contracting Program pursuant to 38 U.S.C. § 8127(c). The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 41 U.S.C. § 3304(a)(5), Authorized or Required by Statute, as implemented by the applicable VA acquisition regulations and deviations. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate with Homefront Security, LLC, 1 Palace Court, Manorville, NY 11949 (SAM UEI: CR4NAABN86C6, CAGE: 80KP8) for this requirement. Homefront Security, LLC has been determined to be an eligible SBA-certified SDVOSB and a capable source for the Brand Name Pelco requirement. The applicable NAICS code is 561621 Security Systems Services (except Locksmiths). Please see the attached solicitation for the complete requirements, instructions, terms, conditions, and applicable response requirements. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTATIONS. THE GOVERNMENT IS NOT SEEKING AND WILL NOT ACCEPT UNSOLICITED QUOTATIONS IN RESPONSE TO THIS NOTICE. THIS NOTICE IS BEING PUBLISHED FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES AND TO SATISFY APPLICABLE SYNOPSIS AND PUBLIC-NOTICE REQUIREMENTS. THE GOVERNMENT INTENDS TO SOLICIT AND NEGOTIATE SOLELY WITH HOMEFRONT SECURITY, LLC UNDER THE VETERANS FIRST CONTRACTING PROGRAM PURSUANT TO 38 U.S.C. § 8127(C). title: RFI/Sources Sought Notice, Heterotrophic Plate Count (HPC) Waterline Testing Services, Biloxi, MS, Pensacola, FL and Panama City Beach, FL
description: 1. PURPOSE The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is conducting market research to identify qualified and interested firms capable of providing routine and surge Heterotrophic Plate Count (HPC) testing of potable waterlines at VA facilities along the Gulf Coast. The Government seeks capability statements from Small Businesses (including SDVOSB/VOSB) and other than small businesses, and from GSA Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) holders under SIN 541380 (Testing Laboratory Services). This RFI/Sources Sought Notice (SSN) is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not obligate the Government to award a contract. 2. BACKGROUND & REGULATORY CONTEXT HPC (Standard Methods 9215) estimates live culturable heterotrophic microorganisms in water and is used to monitor premise plumbing microbiological condition; consistent method/media selection is essential to preserve trend comparability. Short, strict hold times for HPC samples require reliable local logistics (cooling/transport and initiation of analysis within program limits�commonly ?24 hours, and in some jurisdictions ?8 hours for compliance). In healthcare settings, CDC expects facilities to operate comprehensive water management programs; EPA notes HPC can indicate general distribution-system water quality status, and ?500 CFU/mL is used for disinfectant-residual equivalency under SWTR. 3. DRAFT SCOPE OF WORK (SUMMARY) 3.1 Methods Contractor shall perform HPC under Standard Methods (SM) 9215 using acceptable variants (e.g., 9215B, 9215D/R2A, 9215E). Contractor shall document media, incubation temperature, and duration for each sample; the selected method/media shall remain consistent throughout the period of performance for comparability of trends. 3.2 Certifications & Accreditation Contractor shall hold current state certification/accreditation explicitly listing HPC under SM 9215 for the place(s) of performance (e.g., MSDH Drinking Water Laboratory Certification in Mississippi; Florida DOH/NELAP in Florida); ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation covering HPC is preferred. Copies of certificates and scopes must be provided. 3.3 Sample Handling & Logistics Contractor shall provide sampling containers, labels, chain?of?custody (COC) forms, coolers, and transport ice/ice packs; maintain 0�10?�C during transport; prevent freezing. Contractor shall initiate HPC analysis within applicable program hold times and in no case exceed 24 hours from collection unless stricter state limits are applicable. 3.4 Turnaround & Reporting Standard reporting shall be provided within 48 hours of laboratory receipt. Per?sample reports must include sample ID/location, collection and receipt timestamps, method/media/incubation conditions, HPC result in CFU/mL, and QC/batch identifiers. Contractor shall flag and notify the COR for any sample exceeding 500 CFU/mL and provide interpretive notes consistent with EPA guidance. 3.5 Emergency/Surge Capability Contractor shall provide rapid response capability for urgent events (e.g., main breaks, disinfection upsets) and identify surge capacity (peak samples/day) to meet VA needs. 4. ACQUISITION PATHWAYS & MANDATORY SOURCES The Government anticipates competing this requirement via Open Market or GSA MAS SIN 541380 if available. Nothing in this RFI commits the Government to a particular path. 5. SMALL BUSINESS & VETERANS FIRST VA will consider the results of this market research to determine small business set?asides and/or the use of Veterans First authorities. SDVOSB/VOSB respondents should indicate VetCert verification status. Any decision to set aside or use VAAR Subpart 819.70 sole?source authorities (?$5M) will be made at the Government�s discretion and in the best interest of the Government based on market research outcomes. 6. WHAT TO SUBMIT (Capability Statement � 10 pages max) A. Firm Information: Legal name, UEI, CAGE, business size/status (SB, SDVOSB, VOSB, HUBZone, WOSB), primary NAICS (541380) and any relevant NAICS. B. MAS Information (if applicable): GSA MAS contract number; confirmation of SIN 541380 listing; link to eLibrary T&Cs/price list. C. Certifications: Current state certification/accreditation scopes explicitly listing SM 9215 HPC (e.g., MSDH, FL DOH/NELAP) and ISO/IEC 17025 scope (if held). Attach certificates/scopes. D. Methods: Identify SM 9215 variant(s) used (B/D/R2A/E) and your approach to method/media consistency for trend comparability. E. Logistics & TAT: Confirm ability to meet hold?time limits (?24 h minimum; stricter limits prevail) and report within ?48 h; describe courier coverage, latest daily lab receipt times, and COC controls. F. QA/QC: Proficiency testing participation, batch QC practices, and LIMS/portal capabilities for electronic reporting. G. Past Performance: Healthcare water microbiology clients (VA/DoD/hospitals). Provide references (optional). H. Pricing (Non?binding for planning): Rough order?of?magnitude per?sample pricing; field collection fees; surge/expedite rates. 7. GOVERNMENT FURNISHED INFORMATION With any future solicitation, the Government may furnish sampling maps, historical HPC data for trend continuity, and site points of contact. (Not provided at the RFI stage.) 8. Instructions and Response Guidelines: Sources Sought responses are due by September 23, 2026 at 10:00 am (CST) via email to anthony.marion2.gov. All Questions shall be submitted by September 17, 2026 at 10:00 pm (CST) via email to anthony.marion2.gov. Telephone requests or inquires will not be accepted. Public Information will not be provided and shall be utilized to the full extent possible. This a New Requirement. In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the U.S. Government to form a binding contract. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on Contracting Opportunities (https://beta.sam.gov/) website or GSA. It is the responsibility of the interested parties to monitor these sites for additional information pertaining to this Sources Sought, or future RFP/RFQ. 9. DISCLAIMER This RFI is not a request for proposals or quotations. The Government will not reimburse costs incurred for responding. The Government reserves the right to use information provided to inform the acquisition strategy. If a solicitation is issued, it will be posted separately on SAM.gov.

title: Gas Cylinders - Remove, Transport, Dispose
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation that will be issued. Quotations are being requested, and separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 1232SA26Q1502 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for ARS Pacific Basin Agricultural Research Center. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 541620, Environmental Consulting Services. The small business size standard is $19 mil This acquisition is set-aside for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB). All responsible sources may submit a quotation which will be considered by the agency. Statement of Requirement The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), Agricultural Research Service (ARS), Pacific Basin Agricultural Research Center (PBARC), Hilo, Hawaii, requires contractor services to safely remove, characterize (if necessary), transport, and dispose of three (3) compressed gas cylinders with unknown contents (see Figure 1). The cylinders are legacy materials located in a USDA storage building and are no longer required for research operations. Note: The removable steel cylinder caps have become corroded and stuck, making them difficult to remove. Since shipping regulations require tank valves to be accessible, specialized hydraulic equipment may be needed to detach the caps and replace the valves safely. Because the identity and condition of the gases cannot be confirmed by the Government, the contractor shall provide all technical expertise necessary to safely identify (when required), package, transport, and dispose of the cylinders in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local regulations.

Failure to meet these criteria will render the quotation unacceptable. The Government will evaluate recent (completed within the last three years) and relevant past performance to assess the likelihood of successful performance. Past performance will be evaluated on an acceptable or unacceptable basis. The Government may consider offers nonresponsive if they include conditional pricing, price escalation language, or statements indicating that prices are subject to adjustment based on future costs or fees. title: NOI to Sole Source to 10X Genomics
description: The purpose of this requirement is for the acquisition of reagents and consumables required for the Early Detection of Lung Diseases (EDLI) project. These reagents are specifically designed and exclusively compatible with the 10X Genomics Chromium platform, a proprietary system that enables high-resolution gene expression analysis. The EDLI project relies on these reagents to ensure experimental continuity, data accuracy, and reproducibility in studies focused on identifying early biomarkers and understanding the mechanisms of infectious and noninfectious lung diseases. As sole-source items, these reagents cannot be substituted without disrupting ongoing experiments and compromising the integrity of the research. The acquisition will support the project�s critical mission to advance diagnostic and therapeutic approaches for lung diseases. � Product Service Code: 6640 � Laboratory Equipment and Supplies � NAICS Code: 325413 � In-Vitro Diagnostic Substance Manufacturing � Place of Performance: NIH Clinical Center, Bethesda, MD 20892 USA POTS: 26-009308 Description: This is a notice of intent, not a request for a quotation. A solicitation document will not be issued, and quotations will not be requested. The National Institutes of Health (NIH) intends to award a one-year contract to 10X Genomics, located at 6230 Stoneridge Mall Rd, Pleasanton, CA 94588-3260, on a firm fixed price sole source award basis for the acquisition of reagents and consumables required for the Early Detection of Lung Diseases project. The proposed vendor, 10X Genomics, is the sole source for the reagents required for use with the 10X Genomics instrument. Their proprietary reagents are uniquely designed and exclusively compatible with their instrument, ensuring optimal performance and data integrity. This kit is a specialized reagent set designed exclusively for the 10X Genomics Chromium platform/instrument, enabling cutting-edge single-cell and multiomic analyses. The GEM-X Universal 5' Gene Expression v3 Kit facilitates high-resolution gene expression profiling, immune repertoire analysis, and other advanced applications critical to identifying early biomarkers and understanding the molecular mechanisms of infectious and noninfectious lung diseases. These capabilities are essential to achieving the EDLI project�s objectives, which aim to advance diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for lung health. Due to the proprietary nature of the GEM-X Universal 5' Gene Expression v3 and its unique compatibility with the 10X Genomics system, no alternative supplies can meet the technical requirements of the EDLI project. Procuring this kit is essential for ensuring the continuity and success of the research. This acquisition is being conducted using policies unique to the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 13 � Simplified Acquisition Procedures, Subpart 13.106-1(b)(1), For purchases not exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold (SAT), contracting officers may solicit from one source if the contracting officer determines that the circumstance of the contract action deem only one source reasonably available. Contracts awarded using FAR Part 13-Simplified Acquisition Procedures are exempt from the requirements of FAR Part 6-Competition Requirements. The determination by the Government not to compete the proposed requirement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. title: Building Demolition, Norway House, MB
description: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) intends to retain a Contractor to provide construction services for its Norway House decommissioned detachment. The contractor will be responsible for the demolition and disposal of the existing Facility Building, Radio Tower and Tower Foundation. This also includes the demolition and disposal of existing site works including concrete sidewalks and wood parking fencing and the disconnection of existing sewer and water system and capping them at the mains. Electricity is shut off but wiring is still connected to the building. The contract period will be until August 31, 2027. The anticipated start date is November 01, 2026. In order to be considered, a supplier must certify that it qualifies as an Indigenous business as defined under PSIB and that it will comply with all requirements of PSIB. This procurement is set aside from all the trade agreements under the provision each has that permits the procurement to be set aside for Indigenous business. The date, time and location for the Phase Two site visit will be identified during Phase Two. Canada retains the right to negotiate with any supplier on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. It is the sole responsibility of the Bidder to regularly consult GETS for the most up-to-date information. Canada will not be liable for any oversight on the Bidder's part nor for notification services offered by a third party. As a result, the supplier integrity and compliance provisions are being applied in RCMP contracting activities as outlined in this solicitation. title: High Reach Genie Services
description: 09/14/2026 **RFI added to attachments, Update WD, Update price sheet, Update visible version of PWS** This is a solicitation for High Reach Genie Services - FA600626Q0033. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. This requirement is for standard commercial preventative maintenance inspections (annual and quarterly safety compliance checks) and unscheduled mechanical repair services for a fleet of eight (8) specialized aerial boom lifts, scissor lifts, and material handling tow tractors at Westover Air Reserve Base. Based on formal market surveillance, this procurement is set aside 100% for Small Business. A GSA MAS schedule was determined to be a non-viable option due to the critical mission requirement for a 24-hour localized on-site emergency response window, which is not available from national schedule vendors without incurring excessive, non-commercial travel surcharges. Offerors must conform with the complete PWS. Key technical parameters include: Broadened Technician Certifications: Technicians must hold active credentials meeting ANSI/IPAF standards for aerial lift platforms (Genie/JLG), or equivalent commercial mechanical certifications (forklift/automotive drivetrain) for material handling tow tractors (Toyota). Decoupled Emergency Response Timelines: Phase 1 (Notification to On-Site Diagnosis): Contractor technician must arrive on-site within 24 hours of receiving an emergency service call from the Maintenance Flight. Phase 2 (Diagnostics to Estimate Submission): Contractor must submit an itemized repair and parts estimate to the Contracting Officer within 24 business hours of completing the diagnostic visit. Phase 3 (Approval to Final Repair): Contractor must complete the physical repair work within 24 hours of receiving formal electronic approval from the Contracting Officer. Proprietary Parts Sourcing Exemption: For standard parts and commercial consumables, the contractor must supply three (3) competitive quotes. For proprietary Genie or JLG components, the contractor is exempt from the three-quote requirement and may supply a single manufacturer-authorized quote paired with current MSRP catalog listings. Future Equipment Phase-In: The fleet currently contains four active assets, with four additional assets (2 JLG lifts and 2 Toyota tow tractors) currently on order. Offerors will not charge the firm-fixed PM rate for on-order assets. The government will activate the corresponding CLINS (CLINs 0004, 1004, etc.) via administrative modification only once the new equipment is formally accepted. Addendum to RFO FAR 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors � Commercial Products and Commercial Services: Quotes must be submitted electronically to the Contracting Officer via email at robert.stacy.1@us.af.mil no later than September 16, 2026, at 1200 hours EST. The submission must consist of two separate volumes: Sub-Factor 1: Personnel Qualifications. Submit active training records, ANSI/IPAF credentials, or equivalent heavy machinery/drivetrain repair certifications proving technicians are qualified to perform work on commercial-grade boom lifts, scissor lifts, and industrial tow tractors. Sub-Factor 2: Responsive Deployment Plan. Provide a narrative detailing the technician deployment workflow, showing how the contractor will meet the strict 24-hour emergency on-site diagnostic requirement at Westover ARB. Completed Section 2.0 Pricing Tables for the Base Year and all Option Years. All prices must be rounded to the nearest cent. Addendum to RFO FAR 52.212-2, Evaluation � Commercial Products and Commercial Services: The Government will award a single, Firm-Fixed-Price contract to the responsible offeror whose quote represents the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) to the Government. Quotes will be evaluated using a two-step process: Each quote will be evaluated on a Pass/Fail basis against the following technical factors: Factor 1: Personnel Qualifications. Acceptable only if the contractor submits valid ANSI/IPAF, Genie/JLG OEM, or equivalent heavy equipment/automotive drivetrain certifications for all proposed service technicians. Factor 2: Responsive Deployment Plan. Acceptable only if the contractor�s plan demonstrates a clear, logical, and dependable process to get a qualified technician on-site at Westover ARB within 24 hours of notification. Of those quotes determined to be Technically Acceptable, the contract will be awarded to the offeror with the lowest cumulative total price for the Base Year and all Option Years (excluding the future equipment phase-in pool which is preset by the Government). The following RFO FAR and R-DFARS clauses apply to this acquisition and are incorporated by reference: RFO FAR 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors � Commercial Products and Commercial Services (Aug 2026). RFO FAR 52.212-4, Contract Terms and Conditions � Commercial Products and Commercial Services (Aug 2026). RFO FAR 52.217-9, Option to Extend the Term of the Contract (Aug 2026) � Within 30 Days of contract expiration. R-DFARS 252.204-7003, Control of Government Personnel Work Product (Aug 2026). R-DFARS 252.232-7003, Electronic Submission of Payment Requests and Receiving Reports (Aug 2026).

title: Console Desk System
description: This solicitation, W50S72-26-Q-7301, is being issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ). This solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01, effective 13 Mar 2026. The Government intends to award a firm-fixed price (FFP) contract to the vendor whose quote is the lowest price that meets or exceeds the minimum specifications. This procurement is set aside 100% for small business. The NAICS code applicable to this requirement is 337211 and the small business size standard is 1,000 employees. The Government intends to make a single award as a result of this solicitation; however, multiple awards may be made if determined to be in the Government's best interest. Please ensure your SAM profile reflects all socio-economic group(s) and NAICS Codes applicable to your business. title: High-Velocity Water-Cable Safety Barriers and Crash Attenuator Systems
description: 1. Description and Required Regulatory Statements (FAR 12.202(b)(1)(i)) This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 12 (Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services), as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; offers/quotes are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 70LGLY26QGLB00056 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for the procurement and delivery of six hundred and forty-nine (649) portable, water-filled, cable-reinforced longitudinal safety barriers and six (6) compatible, anchorless, water-filled crash attenuator end treatments to support emergency driver training operations on Emergency Response Ranges #7 and #8 at FLETC Glynco, GA. This acquisition is 100% set-aside for Small Business concerns. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference with the same force and effect as if they were given in full text. The full text of FAR and Homeland Security Acquisition Regulation (HSAR) provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at https://www.acquisition.gov. The Defense Priorities and Allocations System (DPAS) assigned rating is Not Applicable. 2. Schedule of Supplies / Services & Quoted Line Items (FAR 12.202(b)(1)(ii)) CLIN 0001 - Water-Filled, Cable-Reinforced Safety Barriers, QTY 649, EA CLIN 0002- Compatible Crash Attenuator End Treatments, Qty 6, EA CLIN 0003-FOB Destination Shipping & Freight, Qty 1, LOT 3. Description of Requirement & Salient Characteristics (FAR 12.202(b)(1)(iii)) A. Background & Operational Scope The Federal Law Enforcement Training Centers (FLETC) requires the direct supply and delivery of high-performance water-filled safety barriers and impact crash cushions to contain, redirect, and safely decelerate errant training vehicles during high-speed emergency response maneuvers on Ranges #7 and #8. This contract is strictly for manufacture, assembly hardware, and delivery; on-site filling, ballasting, and deployment will be accomplished by Government personnel. B. Salient Characteristics for CLIN 0001 (Water-Cable Barriers - Qty: 649) Dimensions: Length: 75" to 76" per section; Height: 43" to 46"; Width: 18" to 22.5". Weights: Empty weight: 160 lbs. to 215 lbs. to allow manual movement prior to filling; Filled ballasted weight: 2,000 lbs. to 2,150 lbs. when ballasted with municipal tap water. Material: Durable, high-density, UV-stabilized polyethylene plastic with molded forklift pass-through pockets and stacking lugs. Internal Cable Reinforcement: Minimum of four (4) integrated, corrosion-resistant internal steel cables running longitudinally through the barrier body, interconnecting section-to-section to establish a continuous high-strength tension line. Connection System: Interlocking multi-knuckle hinge design secured with galvanized steel T-pins and keeper pins, allowing up to 15 degrees of articulation per joint to accommodate track curves. Crash-Test Certification: Independently certified under NCHRP Report 350 and/or AASHTO MASH criteria for Test Level 3 (TL-3) longitudinal barriers at 62.1 mph (100 km/h). Color: High-visibility Orange. C. Salient Characteristics for CLIN 0002 (Crash Attenuators - Qty: 6) Functionality: Gating, non-redirective, water-filled longitudinal impact attenuator (crash cushion) designed to deform, rupture, and absorb impact energy upon frontal collision. Compatibility: Native, manufacturer-approved transition connection hardware that links directly and seamlessly to the CLIN 0001 barrier profile. Dimensions: Overall array length of approximately 25 feet (pin-to-pin) to satisfy TL-3 criteria; system width under 2.3 feet to preserve range shoulder clearance. Anchoring: 100% anchorless system requiring no foundation anchor bolts, concrete anchoring, or drilling into asphalt. Crash-Test Certification: Independently certified under NCHRP Report 350 and/or AASHTO MASH criteria for Test Level 3 (TL-3) crash cushions. Color: High-visibility Yellow. D. Quality & Warranty Standards New Equipment Only: All units, pins, and hardware must be newly manufactured and pristine. Reconditioned, remanufactured, or surplus goods are strictly unacceptable. Commercial Warranty: Minimum one (1) year standard commercial manufacturer warranty covering structural integrity, leakage, UV degradation, and mechanical hardware. Hardware Completeness: All connecting pins, keeper pins, T-pins, and transition hardware necessary for full deployment must be provided in full. 4. Delivery, Acceptance, and FOB Point (FAR 12.202(b)(1)(iv)) FOB Point: Strict FOB Destination (FAR 52.247-34). The contractor retains risk of loss or damage and pays all transportation, fuel surcharges, and transit insurance. Delivery Destination: Federal Law Enforcement Training Centers (FLETC) 1131 Chapel Crossing Road, Building 261 Receiving Glynco, GA 31524 Attn: Emergency Response Ranges #7 and #8 Project Delivery Timeline: Complete delivery within sixty (60) calendar days After Receipt of Order (ARO). Receiving / Offloading: The contractor shall coordinate freight scheduling with advance shipping notices (ASNs). FLETC Glynco will furnish the forklift equipment and operators to unload the flatbed trailers upon arrival. Inspection & Acceptance: Final inspection for physical condition, quantities, and salient compliance will be conducted at destination by the Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR). 5. Evaluation & Basis for Award (Summary of FAR 52.212-2 Addendum) Award will be made on a Best Value Trade-Off basis in accordance with FAR 12.203 and Section M of the solicitation: Evaluation Factors: Factor 1: Technical Capability & Product Quality (Acceptable / Unacceptable based on cut sheets, TL-3 crash test certifications, and salient characteristic compliance). Factor 2: Delivery Schedule & Freight Logistics (Acceptable / Unacceptable based on binding 60-day ARO commitment, ~11 flatbed staging plan, and FOB Destination terms). Factor 3: Price (Evaluated for price completeness, calculation of Total Evaluated Price, and price reasonableness in accordance with FAR 12.209 and FAR 15.404-1). Factor Relative Importance: Non-price factors (Factors 1 and 2), when combined, are significantly more important than Price. Factor 1 is more important than Factor 2. The Government reserves the right to award to a higher-priced offeror if superior technical headroom, enhanced durability, or accelerated delivery warrants paying a price premium. 6. Submission Instructions, Deadlines, and Point of Contact (FAR 12.202(b)(1)(vii)) Submission Method: All quotations must be submitted electronically via email directly to the Contracting Officer: Contracting Officer: Ricardo Soto Email: ricardo.soto@fletc.dhs.gov Subject Line: QUOTE SUBMISSION: 70LGLY26QGLB00060 - Water-Cable Barriers [Vendor Name] Closing Date & Time: Quotations must be received no later than September 23, 2026, at 12:00 PM Eastern Time (ET). Required Submission Documents: Volume I (Technical & Logistics): Signed SF-1449 and amendments (SF-30); 60-day quote validity statement; product cut sheets; dimension drawings; official independent NCHRP-350 / MASH TL-3 crash-test reports or FHWA eligibility letters; commercial warranty; and binding delivery timeline with staging plan. Volume II (Price): Completed pricing for CLINs 0001, 0002, and 0003, with prompt payment or volume discount terms (if applicable). Questions Deadline: Inquiries or clarification requests must be submitted via email no later than September 21, 2026, at 12:00 PM ET. Answers will be disseminated via a formal amendment posted to SAM.gov.

description: 09/16/2026 RFI v2 has been updated to answer new questions. (1330L)...RS 09/16/2026 RFI v2 has been added, which addresses new questions. 09/14/2026 **RFI added to attachments, Update WD, Update price sheet, Update visible version of PWS** This is a solicitation for High Reach Genie Services - FA600626Q0033. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. This requirement is for standard commercial preventative maintenance inspections (annual and quarterly safety compliance checks) and unscheduled mechanical repair services for a fleet of eight (8) specialized aerial boom lifts, scissor lifts, and material handling tow tractors at Westover Air Reserve Base. Based on formal market surveillance, this procurement is set aside 100% for Small Business. A GSA MAS schedule was determined to be a non-viable option due to the critical mission requirement for a 24-hour localized on-site emergency response window, which is not available from national schedule vendors without incurring excessive, non-commercial travel surcharges. Offerors must conform with the complete PWS. Key technical parameters include: Broadened Technician Certifications: Technicians must hold active credentials meeting ANSI/IPAF standards for aerial lift platforms (Genie/JLG), or equivalent commercial mechanical certifications (forklift/automotive drivetrain) for material handling tow tractors (Toyota). Decoupled Emergency Response Timelines: Phase 1 (Notification to On-Site Diagnosis): Contractor technician must arrive on-site within 24 hours of receiving an emergency service call from the Maintenance Flight. Phase 2 (Diagnostics to Estimate Submission): Contractor must submit an itemized repair and parts estimate to the Contracting Officer within 24 business hours of completing the diagnostic visit. Phase 3 (Approval to Final Repair): Contractor must complete the physical repair work within 24 hours of receiving formal electronic approval from the Contracting Officer. Proprietary Parts Sourcing Exemption: For standard parts and commercial consumables, the contractor must supply three (3) competitive quotes. For proprietary Genie or JLG components, the contractor is exempt from the three-quote requirement and may supply a single manufacturer-authorized quote paired with current MSRP catalog listings. Future Equipment Phase-In: The fleet currently contains four active assets, with four additional assets (2 JLG lifts and 2 Toyota tow tractors) currently on order. Offerors will not charge the firm-fixed PM rate for on-order assets. The government will activate the corresponding CLINS (CLINs 0004, 1004, etc.) via administrative modification only once the new equipment is formally accepted. Addendum to RFO FAR 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors � Commercial Products and Commercial Services: Quotes must be submitted electronically to the Contracting Officer via email at robert.stacy.1@us.af.mil no later than September 16, 2026, at 1200 hours EST. The submission must consist of two separate volumes: Sub-Factor 1: Personnel Qualifications. Submit active training records, ANSI/IPAF credentials, or equivalent heavy machinery/drivetrain repair certifications proving technicians are qualified to perform work on commercial-grade boom lifts, scissor lifts, and industrial tow tractors. Sub-Factor 2: Responsive Deployment Plan. Provide a narrative detailing the technician deployment workflow, showing how the contractor will meet the strict 24-hour emergency on-site diagnostic requirement at Westover ARB. Completed Section 2.0 Pricing Tables for the Base Year and all Option Years. All prices must be rounded to the nearest cent. Addendum to RFO FAR 52.212-2, Evaluation � Commercial Products and Commercial Services: The Government will award a single, Firm-Fixed-Price contract to the responsible offeror whose quote represents the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) to the Government. Quotes will be evaluated using a two-step process: Each quote will be evaluated on a Pass/Fail basis against the following technical factors: Factor 1: Personnel Qualifications. Acceptable only if the contractor submits valid ANSI/IPAF, Genie/JLG OEM, or equivalent heavy equipment/automotive drivetrain certifications for all proposed service technicians. Factor 2: Responsive Deployment Plan. Acceptable only if the contractor�s plan demonstrates a clear, logical, and dependable process to get a qualified technician on-site at Westover ARB within 24 hours of notification. Of those quotes determined to be Technically Acceptable, the contract will be awarded to the offeror with the lowest cumulative total price for the Base Year and all Option Years (excluding the future equipment phase-in pool which is preset by the Government). The following RFO FAR and R-DFARS clauses apply to this acquisition and are incorporated by reference: RFO FAR 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors � Commercial Products and Commercial Services (Aug 2026). RFO FAR 52.212-4, Contract Terms and Conditions � Commercial Products and Commercial Services (Aug 2026). RFO FAR 52.217-9, Option to Extend the Term of the Contract (Aug 2026) � Within 30 Days of contract expiration. R-DFARS 252.204-7003, Control of Government Personnel Work Product (Aug 2026). title: Pre-solicitation Notice with Intent to Sole Source � Sportsmobile Texas, Inc.
description: DESCRIPTION The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Farm Production and Conservation (FPAC) Business Center, on behalf of the Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS), intends to award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price contract to Sportsmobile, Inc., located at 9805 Gray Blvd #B, Austin TX 78758-5411. This procurement is conducted in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 12.102(b) for the acquisition of commercial services. The USDA requires upfit services for a Government Furnished 2024 Mercedes Benz Sprinter 170" Extended Cargo Van. Background and Requirement Description: This acquisition is for the design, fabrication, and installation of a custom interior upfit for one Government-furnished 2024 Mercedes-Benz Sprinter 170" Extended 2500 Cargo Van. The completed upfit will convert the vehicle into a specialized Mobile Engineering Field Laboratory and Quality Assurance Command Center for USDA-FPAC-NRCS-Texas watershed infrastructure projects.and servicing functions, and manage the active Farm Loan Programs (FLP) portfolio. The required upfit includes insulation, a cab partition/bulkhead with walkthrough opening, heavy-duty commercial flooring, integrated workstation and cabinetry, specialized shelving and soil sample storage, auxiliary power and climate control systems, galley and water systems, durable interior finishes, and safety features. The upfit must preserve safe vehicle handling and weight distribution due to the Sprinter van�s extended rear overhang and 2500 GVWR. The completed vehicle will enable USDA-NRCS engineers, watershed construction project managers, and inspectors to conduct field-based soil testing, maintain sample integrity, secure sensitive equipment, review project documentation, and perform real-time quality assurance activities at remote watershed construction sites. Sole Source Justification: The Government�s requirement is for a highly specialized custom upfit of a government furnished 2024 Mercedes-Benz Sprinter 170" Extended 2500 Cargo Van into a mobile engineering field laboratory for USDA-FPAC-NRCS-Texas watershed infrastructure projects. This requirement is not a standard van interior build or general recreational vehicle conversion. The upfit must support field engineering, soil sample testing, secure transport of sensitive equipment, and real-time quality assurance functions at remote watershed construction sites. Sportsmobile Texas, Inc. demonstrated the technical expertise, engineering capability, and relevant industry experience to perform the custom design, fabrication, and installation required for this project. Market research showed that Sportsmobile Texas, Inc. can meet the Government�s specific technical requirements, including platform-specific weight distribution, custom laboratory layout, secure storage for field testing equipment and soil samples, a heavy-duty walkthrough cab partition, auxiliary power systems, water systems, durable field-use materials, and safety-focused installation. The requirement is unique because it combines vehicle upfitting, mobile laboratory functionality, secure transport of sensitive engineering equipment, rugged field use, and platform-specific design constraints for a government furnished 2024 Mercedes-Benz Sprinter 170" Extended 2500 Cargo Van. Other vendors reviewed during market research did not demonstrate the same ability to meet the complete integrated requirement without compromising the Government�s need for safety, functionality, storage security, weight distribution, or field laboratory capability. Instructions to Industry: This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. All responsible sources who believe they can provide the capability may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which may be considered by the agency. Interested vendors must demonstrate how they can provide the required services and demonstrate their capability to meet the complete integrated requirement without compromising the Government�s need for safety, functionality, storage security, weight distribution, or field laboratory capability. Capability statements must be submitted electronically to the Contract Specialist no later than September 23, 2026, at 12:00 PM EST.

title: Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging (BLSA) image processing services.
description: Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging (BLSA) image processing services. This is a Notice of Intent to Sole Source (NOI), not a request for proposal. The National Cancer Institute intends to negotiate on an other-than-full-and-open competition basis with Department of Electrical Engineering Vanderbilt University, Director of the Center for Computational Imaging Vanderbilt University Institute of Image Science, 2301 Vanderbilt Place, PO Box 351679 Station B, Nashville, TN 37235-1679 for BLSA neuroimaging data. Vanderbilt University Director has developed methods for two unified regression and inference approaches, model II regression and regression calibration, for use in massively univariate inference with imaging data. These methods use the design matrix paradigm and account for both random and non-random imaging regressors. The staff are uniquely experienced with these methods and their application to BLSA data. These methods, as well as other customized scripts written for BLSA data. In addition, the Director and staff have substantial experience in segmentation and analysis of muscle and fat in both MRI and CT images. The Subject matter expert is uniquely qualified to accomplish the goals and to meet the timetable for deliverables given his prior development of code required and quantitative analysis for the specified image processing and longitudinal analyses, as required for continuity of BLSA research. This acquisition involves continuing work on BLSA multi-modal longitudinal image analysis for which the subject matter expert has demonstrated excellent past performance and innovation. While this pre-solicitation does not constitute a solicitation, interested vendors may identify their interest and capability to satisfy this requirement. However, vendors who believe that they can provide the capability required to fully meet the Government's requirement may submit a capabilities statement, including past performance, in writing to the identified point of contact prior to the closing date and time of this notice. Such documentation shall be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct this procurement on a competitive basis. description: This is a notice of intent to award a sole source contract. Pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulations FAR 13.106-1(b)(1)(i). The Embassy of the United States of America in Lome, Togo has a requirement to replace the chiller coils at the Embassy building. The Embassy requires the immediate removal of existing compromised and corroded HVAC chiller coils and the installation of new, direct-fit replacement coils on the facility�s chiller systems. The scope of this project involves the procurement, delivery, and installation of commercial-grade chiller coils to restore the facility's HVAC cooling capacity and efficiency. The Embassy of the United States Lome, Department of State intends to award a firm-fixed-price contract on a sole-source basis to: Johnson Controls Industries � YORK & SABROE Service 14 Rue de Bel Air - 44470 - Carquefou FRANCE Phone number: +33.240.30.63.70 - +33.611.95.75.71 The scope of this acquisition requires from the contractor to provide all labor, supervision, materials, equipment, tools, and transportation necessary to perform the following core tasks: Field verify existing dimensions, configurations, and performance specifications of the current chiller coils. Safely recover and dispose of existing refrigerants in accordance with EPA regulations. Demolish and remove the damaged or degraded cooling coils. Supply and install new, heavy-duty replacement coils matching or exceeding original equipment manufacturer (OEM) performance standards. Reconnect all piping, controls, and electrical components. Perform pressure testing, vacuum pull-down, refrigerant charging, and comprehensive system startup testing to verify proper operation. The anticipated period of performance is three months Place of Performance: US Embassy Lome 4332 blvd Eyadema � Cit� OUA BP 852 Lome Togo Statutory Authority This procurement is being conducted in accordance with FAR Part 13, Simplified Acquisition Procedures. This contract action is for supplies and services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of: Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 13.106-1(b)(1)(i), "Soliciting from a Single Source" for purchases not exceeding the Simplified Acquisition Threshold. Justification for Single Source Johnson Controls (JCI) is uniquely qualified and is the only known source capable of fulfilling this requirement because the rusted coils are part of an existing JCI / York Air Handling Unit (AHU) or Chiller. Replacing them with third-party, non-OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer) coils introduces a high risk of improper alignment, sizing mismatches, and compromised structural integrity. The existing air handling infrastructure relies on proprietary dimensions and specific engineering design thresholds unique to Johnson Controls. Utilizing an aftermarket coil would modify the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) configuration, altering the precise static pressure drop, air velocity profiles, and thermal performance parameters engineered by JCI. The vendor possesses proprietary rights, data software, or manufacturing drawings essential to completing the work. Capability Statements and Responses THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES; AND NO SOLICITATION IS AVAILABLE. Inquiries will only be accepted via email to the Primary Point of Contact: LomeProcurement@state.gov

description: The United States Department of Agriculture, Office of Chief Information Officer, Digital Infrastructure Services Center (DISC) intends to award a purchase order on a Sole Source bases to Chicago Soft for the RENEWAL of our current MVS/QuickRef Mainframe Software. The USDA mainframe platform relies on these specific tools and cannot function without their maintenance and support. Chicago Soft, LTD. is the proprietary owner of these software products. MVS/Quick-Ref is a mainframe product that provides instant online access to message descriptions and programming information on MVS systems. As licensed products, this software is proprietary and has various legal restrictions for use and maintenance. Only the software developer has the rights to the source code. title: DirecTV based Cable Headend System Maintenance and Repair
description: ***Amendment posted to answer questions and extend due date and time.*** The Ohio National Guard (OHARNG) owns and operates a DirecTV based cable headend system. The OHARNG maintains a service contract with DirecTV for television services. Facilitating this service provider is a requirement. The core components of the headend system are failing and require replacement. The OHARNG requires the procurement of the following line items. 1: Quantity of 4 (four) - HDMI MPEG2 digital video encoders specification to match ZeeVee Hdbridge HDb2840-NA 4-CH 2: Quantity 16 (sixteen) - DirecTV receivers specifications to match DIRECTV H26 RECEIVER. 3: Quantity 1 (one) - Off-air ATSC to QAM modulator specifications to match DT-ATSC-QAM-8V2 Off-Air ATSC Over Air signal modulator, to DIRECTV six line trunk amp. 4: Quantity 1 (one) - Line amps DIRECTV SWM 30, new DirecTV receivers and SWM amps as necessary for coax distribution. 5: Quantity 2 (two) - Rack shelf for tuners, RACK SHELF H26, new rack shelves for new DirecTV receivers and SWM amps as necessary for coax distribution. Installation services: The OHARNG requires the installation of above components and integration into the existing Cable TV headend system. Installation services must include new rack shelves for new DirecTV receivers and SWM amps as necessary for coax distribution. The requirement includes replacement of all ZeeVee 2540 modulators with new ZeeVee 2840 HD input modulators (or matching specification equipment) and program with new H26 DIRECTV HD receivers. Replace ATSC antenna modulators and program off air signals. Setup off-air channels and integrate with DirecTV channel lineup. Balance outputs to appropriately service building coax distribution network. Questions regarding this solicitation must be submitted via email only no later than 12:00 PM (Eastern Time), 14 SEPT 2026, to paul.s.robinson6.civ@army.mil and/or brett.a.fruth.civ@army.mil. title: High Reach Genie Services
description: This is a solicitation for High Reach Genie Services - FA600626Q0033. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. This requirement is for standard commercial preventative maintenance inspections (annual and quarterly safety compliance checks) and unscheduled mechanical repair services for a fleet of eight (8) specialized aerial boom lifts, scissor lifts, and material handling tow tractors at Westover Air Reserve Base. Based on formal market surveillance, this procurement is set aside 100% for Small Business. A GSA MAS schedule was determined to be a non-viable option due to the critical mission requirement for a 24-hour localized on-site emergency response window, which is not available from national schedule vendors without incurring excessive, non-commercial travel surcharges. Offerors must conform with the complete PWS. Key technical parameters include: Broadened Technician Certifications: Technicians must hold active credentials meeting ANSI/IPAF standards for aerial lift platforms (Genie/JLG), or equivalent commercial mechanical certifications (forklift/automotive drivetrain) for material handling tow tractors (Toyota). Decoupled Emergency Response Timelines: Phase 1 (Notification to On-Site Diagnosis): Contractor technician must arrive on-site within 24 hours of receiving an emergency service call from the Maintenance Flight. Phase 2 (Diagnostics to Estimate Submission): Contractor must submit an itemized repair and parts estimate to the Contracting Officer within 24 business hours of completing the diagnostic visit. Phase 3 (Approval to Final Repair): Contractor must complete the physical repair work within 24 hours of receiving formal electronic approval from the Contracting Officer. Proprietary Parts Sourcing Exemption: For standard parts and commercial consumables, the contractor must supply three (3) competitive quotes. For proprietary Genie or JLG components, the contractor is exempt from the three-quote requirement and may supply a single manufacturer-authorized quote paired with current MSRP catalog listings. Future Equipment Phase-In: The fleet currently contains four active assets, with four additional assets (2 JLG lifts and 2 Toyota tow tractors) currently on order. Offerors will not charge the firm-fixed PM rate for on-order assets. The government will activate the corresponding CLINS (CLINs 0004, 1004, etc.) via administrative modification only once the new equipment is formally accepted. Addendum to RFO FAR 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors � Commercial Products and Commercial Services: Quotes must be submitted electronically to the Contracting Officer via email at robert.stacy.1@us.af.mil no later than September 16, 2026, at 1200 hours EST. The submission must consist of two separate volumes: Sub-Factor 1: Personnel Qualifications. Submit active training records, ANSI/IPAF credentials, or equivalent heavy machinery/drivetrain repair certifications proving technicians are qualified to perform work on commercial-grade boom lifts, scissor lifts, and industrial tow tractors. Sub-Factor 2: Responsive Deployment Plan. Provide a narrative detailing the technician deployment workflow, showing how the contractor will meet the strict 24-hour emergency on-site diagnostic requirement at Westover ARB. Completed Section 2.0 Pricing Tables for the Base Year and all Option Years. All prices must be rounded to the nearest cent. Addendum to RFO FAR 52.212-2, Evaluation � Commercial Products and Commercial Services: The Government will award a single, Firm-Fixed-Price contract to the responsible offeror whose quote represents the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) to the Government. Quotes will be evaluated using a two-step process: Each quote will be evaluated on a Pass/Fail basis against the following technical factors: Factor 1: Personnel Qualifications. Acceptable only if the contractor submits valid ANSI/IPAF, Genie/JLG OEM, or equivalent heavy equipment/automotive drivetrain certifications for all proposed service technicians. Factor 2: Responsive Deployment Plan. Acceptable only if the contractor�s plan demonstrates a clear, logical, and dependable process to get a qualified technician on-site at Westover ARB within 24 hours of notification. Of those quotes determined to be Technically Acceptable, the contract will be awarded to the offeror with the lowest cumulative total price for the Base Year and all Option Years (excluding the future equipment phase-in pool which is preset by the Government). The following RFO FAR and R-DFARS clauses apply to this acquisition and are incorporated by reference: RFO FAR 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors � Commercial Products and Commercial Services (Aug 2026). RFO FAR 52.212-4, Contract Terms and Conditions � Commercial Products and Commercial Services (Aug 2026). RFO FAR 52.217-9, Option to Extend the Term of the Contract (Aug 2026) � Within 30 Days of contract expiration. R-DFARS 252.204-7003, Control of Government Personnel Work Product (Aug 2026). R-DFARS 252.232-7003, Electronic Submission of Payment Requests and Receiving Reports (Aug 2026).

This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number FA8601-26-Q-0150 is issued as a request for quotation (RFQ), for the purchase of a commercial steam boiler and dual kettle system, in accordance with the SOW listed in the attachments. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. NOTE 2: In accordance with R-DFARS 252.204-7021 and R-DFARS 252.204-7025, a CMMC Level 1 assessment is the mandatory minimum requirement for all offerors bidding with the Department of War. It is the responsibility of the offeror to ensure that the quote and its attachments are received. Any correspondence sent via e-mail must contain the subject line �FA860126Q0150 Treatment Chairs�. The entire quotation must be contained in a single e-mail that does not exceed 5 megabytes including attachments, if any. E-mails with compressed files are not permitted. Note that e-mail filters at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base are designed to filter e-mails without subject lines or with suspicious subject lines or contents (i.e., .exe or .zip files). title: NAWCAD WOLF Mission Systems Integration (MSI)
description: DISCLAIMER: THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. This Sources Sought is a market research tool being used to determine potential and eligible business firms that are capable of providing the services described herein prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a Request for Proposal. The existing contract was previously competed, with two offers received. Nevertheless, the Government would like to ensure that there is adequate competition for this procurement. Additionally, the results of this sources sought will also be utilized to determine if any Small Business Set-Aside opportunities exist. All interested large and small businesses are encouraged to respond with a capability statement, but only those businesses or teaming arrangements that are considered small under NAICS 541330-1 will be considered for small business set-aside decisions. INTRODUCTION The Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD) Webster Outlying Field (WOLF) at Patuxent River, MD announces its intention to procure, on a competitive basis services to provide Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Cyber, Combat Systems, Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (C6ISR) integration and installation; systems engineering support; In-Service Engineering Agent (ISEA); and logistics support to Mission Systems programs, systems, and technological areas within the SAIW project portfolio. Further details are provided in the Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS)/Statement of Work (SOW) attached to this synopsis (Attachment 1). The services are currently being performed by The MIL Corporation of Bowie, MD under N00421-24-D-0002. The current contract is Cost-Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF) containing both performance-based Completion CLINs and Level-of-Effort (LOE) CLINs. This contract is due to expire 14-FEB-2029. Although the current Period of Performance (PoP) of this requirement is scheduled to end Q2 FY2029, the estimated exhaustion date is now within Q1 FY2028. PROGRAM BACKGROUND As the organic Lead Systems Integrator� (oLSI�) for the Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD), Webster Outlying Field (WOLF) operates under a product-based business model whereby NAWCAD WOLF civilians lead and manage the execution of the requirements with combined Government-Industry teams. Using this oLSI� approach, the Government maintains control of intellectual property and data rights, enabling WOLF to rapidly adapt solutions to the dynamic needs of the warfighter. The NAWCAD WOLF Ship & Air Integrated Warfare (SAIW) Division is the oLSI� providing design, procurement, integration, testing, and training of Command, Control, Communications, Computers, and Intelligence (C4I) electronic systems that meet the requirements of the United States Navy operating forces. The SAIW Division, operating under the oLSI� model, has requirements for services to provide Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Cyber, Combat Systems, Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance integration and installation (C6ISR); systems engineering support; In-Service Engineering Agent; and logistics support to Mission Systems programs, systems, and technological areas within the SAIW project portfolio. REQUIREMENTS Please review Attachment 1, Draft PWS/SOW and Attachment 2, Draft Hours. If your company has any questions about the PWS/SOW, Draft Hours, or any areas that may need further explanation, please also identify those in the response. The labor categories anticipated to execute the contemplated effort are included in Attachment 2, Draft Hours. Since the resultant contract will be a cost-type effort, the successful awardee will also be required to have a Government approved accounting system upon award. All Contractors that propose must either have or be able to obtain a TOP SECRET facility clearance. A DD Form 254 Contract Security Classification Specification shall apply to this requirement and the prime contractor shall have a �Top Secret� Facility Clearance and a �Secret� Safeguarding Clearance. ELIGIBILITY The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code for this requirement is 541330-1 Engineering Services with a Small Business Size standard of $47 Million. Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capabilities statement. The Product Service Code (PSC) for this effort will be K058: Modification of Equipment - Communication, Detection, and Coherent Radiation Equipment PLACE OF PERFORMANCE % On-Site Government % Off-Site Contractor WOLF St. Ingioes, MD 100% 22% 78% ANTICIPATED CONTRACT TYPE The requirement is anticipated to be a Single Award, Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (SA IDIQ) contract with Cost-Plus-Award-Fee (CPAF) Level of Effort (LOE)/Term Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs) for a portion of labor, Firm Fixed Price (FFP) CLINs for the remaining labor, and cost reimbursable CLINs for Other Direct Costs (ODCs). The proposed contract is anticipated to include tasking and labor categories that are subject to the Service Contract Act. ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE It is anticipated that the resultant contract is estimated to begin in Q1 FY2028 and will have a five-year ordering period It is anticipated performance will commence approximately in December 2027. The estimated manhours hours by CLIN type are as follows: For the FFP CLINs: 272,910 manhours (for estimating purposes only, based on projections from historical data.) For the CPAF CLINs: 892,097 manhours SUBMITTAL INFORMATION It is requested that interested businesses submit to the contracting office a brief capabilities statement package (no more than 15 pages in length, single spaced, 12 point font minimum) demonstrating the ability to perform the effort listed in the attached Draft PWS/SOW, Attachment 1. This documentation must address, at a minimum, the following: Title of the PWS/SOW to which you are responding; Company profile to include number of employees, annual revenue history, office location(s), CAGE code, DUNS number, and a statement regarding current small/large business status; Respondents to this notice must also indicate whether they qualify as a Small, Small Disadvantaged, Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, Women-Owned, 8(a), Historically Underutilized Business (HUB) Zone, or Veteran Owned Small Business concern; If a small business, provide an explanation of your company's ability or your company�s ability combined with a similarly situated entity�s ability to perform at least 50% of the tasking described in this PWS/SOW; Resources available such as corporate management and currently employed personnel to be assigned to tasks under this effort to include professional qualifications, specific experience of such personnel, and the ability to have personnel located at the city specified; Management approach to staffing this effort with qualified personnel; Statement regarding capability to obtain the required industrial security clearances for personnel; Company's ability to meet the requirements in the Facility and Safeguarding requirements; Company's ability to begin performance upon contract award; Company's ability to manage a team of subcontractors, including a list of contracts and teaming arrangements; Prior/current corporate experience performing efforts of similar size and scope within the last three years, including contract number, organization supported, indication of whether as a prime or subcontract
